newsitem.title: USA: No near-term plans for muni trading system - CBOT.
newsitem.headline: No near-term plans for muni trading system - CBOT.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade has scrapped any near-term plans to develop a municipal bond electronic trading system, but would support an outside vendor's attempt to develop one, an official there said Tuesday.

"If the cash market feels there is a great need, and wants it, we would encourage their development of it and endorse a preferred one perhaps," Steve Sural, a group manager for CBOT's financial markets group said. "But we don't have the resources."

The idea to develop an electronic trading system for the 40 bonds underlying the municipal futures contract emerged from a July meeting between CBOT officials and members of a municipal industry council. It was hoped such a system could add transparency.
Grumbling over perceived market manipulation surrounded last year's expiration of the June futures contract, though CBOT officials said the July meeting was not called to address those concerns.
Sural said cash market participants' reponse to a proposed trading system varied, but all acknowledged the difficulty in setting one up, Sural said.
While the CBOT "is not in the business of developing cash market screens," Sural contacted some major data vendors including Reuters to gage their interest in developing one.
Sural received a better reponse from smaller fixed-income industry specific vendors.

"They came out of the woodwork, and said we'd love to develop a system for you," he said. While CBOT is still looking at smaller vendors, "we're still in the process of gathering information to see whether or not it's feasible."
Major trading houses tend to have their own proprietary screens to serve their customers, Sural said.
"Whether those screens get expanded to other players is the issue," he said. "The technology is there."

Providing a supporting role for such an system would be the best allocation of CBOT resources, he said. Ideally, a potential trading system would go beyond the 40 bonds that underlie the municipal bond futures contract.
Sural emphasized that the CBOT continues to concentrate on implementing proposed changes for the municipal futures contract.
One proposal would increase the minimum issue size of bonds in the index to as high as $75 million to $100 million from the current minimum of $50 million.
Another would expand the evaluation time for determining whether to delete bonds from the index due to illiquidity. The time frame would increase to 20 to 30 days, versus the current 15 days.
A third proposal would allow bonds deleted from the index to return to it provided they meet its criteria.

The CBOT is currently working out some technical wrinkles with a "data provider" that Sural declined to indentify. After those matters are sorted out, the plan will proceed to the Commodities Futures Trading Commission for its review, he said.
